text:
Alex: Heads-up — nightly matmul perf regression on v0.43 targeting GPU-pool-A. Observed ~12% tail latency increase vs yesterday on short seq (<16) workloads. Repro locally with our 8-token warmup trace.
PerfBot: ALERT: regression detected for job matmul-nightly (run/172500). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/172500 — notable uptick in p95. :warning:
Priya: Can you attach the nsys / nvprof traces and the inference config (batch sizes, splitK enabled/threshold, quantization)? Also driver/cuBLAS versions.
Alex: Uploads: s3://redwood/traces/matmul/172500_nsys.qtrace and nvprof dump at s3://redwood/traces/matmul/172500_nvprof.txt. Config: batch=8, max_tokens=16, split_k_threshold=64 (default), quant=fp16, cuBLASLt 11.9. We also ran a quick nvprof snippet: ```
== NVPROF (sample) ==
Kernel: cublasLtMatmul, algo=45, time=2.1ms, workspace=4096
Kernel: cublasLtMatmul, algo=71, time=3.2ms, workspace=16777216
Kernel: cublasLtMatmul, algo=15, time=4.0ms, workspace=33554432
Note: runtime chose algo=15 for a subset of launches after commit abc123.
```
Sam: I think abc123 (batching heuristic tweak) flipped the splitK decision for some shapes. That forces cuBLASLt into the split-K family, which our kernel-selection now maps to algo families with higher workspace. TL;DR: different logical split leads to different algo families. Link: https://git.internal/r/commits/abc123
Jen: Perfetto shows a clear pattern: a few launches go into algo=15 and immediately trigger a cudaMallocAsync path that can't service the request and falls back to sync malloc -> serialization. Timeline snippet: ```
[0.000s] H2D async memcpy (batch 1)
[0.002s] cublasLtMatmul launch (algo=15) -> workspace query -> need 32MB
[0.0022s] cudaMallocAsync backlog -> fallback to synchronous cudaMalloc -> stall
[0.003s] memcpy waits -> kernel enqueue delayed -> downstream batches serialized
```
Priya: That matches the p95 spike. Hypothesis: workspace query frontier returns candidate algo list, we pick the fastest (algo=15) but it requires large workspace that the async allocator can't satisfy under current pool fragmentation. The allocation syncs and wins CPU time -> tail latency.
Alex: Quick experiment: set env CUBLASLT_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=8388608 (8MB) and reran the same workload. Result: p95 regression disappears (~0.8% diff). Logs show selection stopped hitting algo=15 and picked algo=45/71 which have much smaller workspace.
Sam: Sounds good. Two action items: 1) Short-term: enforce a workspace cap in the runtime for latency-sensitive routes (config flag + env override). 2) Medium: revert the splitK flip from abc123 or make it contingent on warmup + allocator health. I'll open a PR for (1).
Jen: Also propose: add a small telemetry counter for "workspace_requested_bytes" per-request in Console so we can alert when avg workspace > X. That would have caught this faster.
Priya: Can we also add a perf test that runs short-seq matmul through the nightly bench to catch this class of reg? Add an nvprof/nsys smoke target that asserts no algo requiring > 16MB selected for <32-token shapes.
Alex: I'll attach the minimal repro and a failing test case to the issue. Opening issue: https://issues.redwood/INF-1427 with traces and perfetto screenshots.
PerfBot: Created issue INF-1427 and linked to PR draft #560 by Sam.
Sam: I'll run a full nsys sweep on GPU-pool-A with the workspace cap and post results here when done.
Jen: I'll draft the batching tweak and a note for the oncall about rollback if we see allocator thrash.
Alex: Thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for now. Follow-ups are in INF-1427 and PR #560. :thumbsup:
